note: Facts and sources behind the member descriptions in NE.json, gathered 2026-10-05. "review" holds research notes for a human check; "issues" lists open questions.

byways.name: 385 - Gold Rush Byway
byways.where: US 385, South Dakota line to Colorado line per NDOT (158 mi); Visit Nebraska describes Chadron to Sidney (131 mi). Dawes, Box Butte, Morrill, Cheyenne counties

facts.fact: NDOT lists it as 158 miles along US 385 through the Panhandle from South Dakota to Colorado.
In the 1870s more than $200,000 in gold a day traveled the route.
Courthouse and Jail Rocks near Bridgeport rise more than 240 feet above Pumpkin Creek; Carhenge at Alliance is built from 39 painted cars; Chadron State Park dates from 1921.

byways.review: Lengths disagree: NDOT 158 mi state line to state line, Visit Nebraska 131 mi Chadron to Sidney, catalog line 180 mi.

byways.name: Bridges to Buttes Byway
byways.where: US 20, Valentine west to the Wyoming line near Harrison (197 mi); Cherry, Sheridan, Dawes, Sioux counties

facts.fact: NDOT lists it as 197 miles from Valentine west to the Wyoming border on US 20.
The route crosses rolling Sandhills in the east and prairie in the northern Panhandle, through Merriman, Gordon, Rushville, Chadron and Crawford to Harrison.
Toadstool Geologic Park, north of Crawford, has unusual rock formations and fossil deposits; the Harrison House Hotel was built in 1886 by the Chicago & North Western railroad.

byways.name: Heritage Highway
byways.where: US 136, Brownville on the Missouri River west to Edison (238 mi), ten counties

facts.fact: NDOT lists it as 238 miles from historic Brownville on the Missouri River to Edison on US 136.
Towns along it include Auburn, Beatrice, Fairbury, Hebron, Superior, Red Cloud and Alma; Brownville has about 150 people.

Stops include Homestead National Historical Park at Beatrice, Oregon and California trail wagon ruts at Rock Creek Station, and Willa Cather's childhood home in Red Cloud, a National Historic Landmark.

byways.name: Lewis & Clark Scenic Byway
byways.where: US 75, north of Omaha to South Sioux City (82 mi per NDOT; Visit Nebraska says 98 mi from Omaha); Douglas, Washington, Burt, Thurston, Dakota counties

facts.fact: NDOT lists it as 82 miles from just north of Omaha to South Sioux City along US 75.
The road follows the Missouri River through cropland and wooded bluffs, by Fort Calhoun, Blair, Tekamah and Winnebago.

Fort Atkinson State Historical Park at Fort Calhoun once held a quarter of the US Army; the route crosses the Winnebago Tribe of Nebraska's reservation, which holds an annual Homecoming Celebration powwow.

byways.review: Lengths disagree: NDOT 82 mi, Visit Nebraska 98 mi (counted from Omaha), catalog line 77 mi.

byways.name: Lincoln Highway Scenic & Historic Byway
byways.designation: Nebraska Scenic Byway; National Scenic Byway
byways.where: US 30 across the state, Blair (Iowa side) to Kimball and the Wyoming line (400 mi per NDOT, 450 per Visit Nebraska)

facts.fact: NDOT lists it as 400 miles along US 30, America's first coast-to-coast route, from border to border, and marks it as awarded National Scenic Byway.
Visit Nebraska gives 450 miles from Blair to Kimball through Fremont, Columbus, Grand Island, Kearney, Lexington, Gothenburg, North Platte, Ogallala and Sidney.
Gothenburg has a Pony Express station; Columbus has the Andrew Jackson Higgins National Memorial with a full-size landing craft replica.

byways.review: Lengths disagree: NDOT 400 mi, Visit Nebraska 450 mi, catalog line 451 mi. 'Still standing' rests on Visit Nebraska listing the station as a visitable stop.

byways.name: Loup Rivers Scenic Byway
byways.where: NE 11 and NE 91, Wood River to Dunning (150 mi); Hall, Howard, Greeley, Valley, Garfield, Loup, Blaine counties

facts.fact: NDOT lists it as 150 miles along Nebraska Highways 11 and 91 from Wood River to Dunning.
The route follows the North Loup River past red barns and silos through Dannebrog, Scotia, Ord, Elyria, Burwell and Brewster.

Happy Jack Chalk Mine at Scotia is described as the only publicly accessible chalk room-and-pillar mine in North America; Fort Hartsuff State Historical Park is near Elyria; Calamus Reservoir is near Burwell.

byways.name: Outlaw Trail Scenic Byway
byways.where: NE 12, near South Sioux City west to Valentine (231 mi); Dakota, Dixon, Cedar, Knox, Boyd, Keya Paha, Cherry counties

facts.fact: NDOT lists it as 231 miles from near South Sioux City to Valentine on Nebraska Highway 12.
Towns include Ponca, Wynot, Crofton, Niobrara, Springview and Sparks; Monowi, where Elsie Eiler is the sole resident and mayor, is billed as the nation's smallest town.
Smith Falls State Park has the highest waterfall in the state; the route passes Lewis and Clark Lake and the Niobrara National Scenic River.

byways.review: Catalog name is 'Outlaw Trail'; NDOT and Visit Nebraska call it Outlaw Trail Scenic Byway.

byways.name: Sandhills Journey Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Nebraska Scenic Byway; National Scenic Byway
byways.where: NE 2, Grand Island to Alliance (272 mi); via Ravenna, Broken Bow, Dunning, Halsey, Thedford, Mullen, Hyannis

facts.fact: NDOT lists it as 272 miles on Nebraska Highway 2 from Grand Island to Alliance and marks it as awarded National Scenic Byway.
The route crosses one of the world's largest areas of grass-stabilized sand dunes and passes the Nebraska National Forest; sandhill cranes migrate through in spring.
Towns include Ravenna, Broken Bow, Dunning, Halsey, Thedford, Mullen and Hyannis; Broken Bow has a visitor center in a farmhouse-style red barn.

byways.name: Western Trails Scenic & Historic Byway
byways.where: US 26 and NE 92, Ogallala northwest to the Wyoming line (144 mi); Keith, Garden, Morrill, Scotts Bluff counties

facts.fact: NDOT lists it as a 144-mile route from Ogallala northwest to the Wyoming border along US 26 and Nebraska Highway 92.
The byway traces the Oregon Trail and the Texas Trail up the North Platte River valley through Lewellen, Oshkosh, Bridgeport, Bayard and Gering.
Sites include Lake McConaughy, Ash Hollow State Historical Park, Chimney Rock National Historic Site and Scotts Bluff National Monument, where wagon ruts and Mitchell Pass can be seen.

issues: visitnebraska.com returns 403 to curl; pages were read with WebFetch and loaded normally there.

Route lengths disagree between NDOT, Visit Nebraska and the catalog lines for Gold Rush (158 / 131 / 180 mi), Lewis & Clark (82 / 98 / 77 mi) and Lincoln Highway (400 / 450 / 451 mi). Gold Rush: NDOT says state line to state line, Visit Nebraska says Chadron to Sidney; worth checking whether the catalog line runs past Chadron or Sidney as expected.
Western Trails: NDOT 144 mi vs catalog line 181 mi; Bridges to Buttes, Heritage, Sandhills Journey match closely; Loup Rivers 150 vs 141; Outlaw Trail 231 vs 244.

National Scenic Byway status of Lincoln Highway (NE) and Sandhills Journey comes from NDOT and Visit Nebraska; the catalog lists both only as Nebraska State Scenic Byway, so the designations field may need 'National Scenic Byway' added (not checked against FHWA, WebSearch budget exhausted).
No byway has its own official page other than Visit Nebraska; NDOT gives no per-byway pages.
No second program: the brief lists no USFS, BLM or other catalog roads in Nebraska.
